No. The original definition of 'representative' is limited to "an employee or an agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that investment adviser" (Passage A). The 2020‑amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' expands the scope to include "any member, partner, officer, director or employee or any sales staff ... including any person occupying a similar status or performing a similar function ... engaged in providing investment advisory services" and explicitly adds client‑facing roles while excluding only non‑client‑facing clerical staff (Passage B). Therefore the two definitions do not cover the same set of persons; the 2020 definition is broader.

answer: Yes, the April 16 transaction is permissible. Regulation 15(7) bars the adviser from transacting contrary to its advice for fifteen days from the advice date, but allows a transaction if a revised assessment is given at least 24 hours before the transaction. The original sell advice was on 1 April, so the fifteen‑day period ends on 15 April; the intended purchase on 16 April is after that period. A revised assessment was issued on 14 April, which is more than 24 hours before the 16 April transaction. Therefore both conditions are satisfied and the transaction is allowed.

citations.quote: Regulation 15(7): An investment advisor shall not enter into transactions on its own account which is contrary to its advice given to clients for a period of fifteen days from the day of such advice. Provided that during the period of such fifteen days, if the investment adviser is of the opinion that the situation has changed, then it may enter into such a transaction on its own account after giving such revised assessment to the client at least 24 hours in advance of entering into such transaction.
